mappings.applicability_reason: This requirement concerns privileged administrative or operator interfaces, but threat thr-001 involves only the automated Callback Receiver webhook endpoint and the Channel Poster service processing payment provider callbacks into channel messages; no operator-facing administrative interface appears in the described attack path, so it does not bear on this threat.

req-AI-001 applies where the system passes externally sourced content to a model. The Order Notifier context and thr-001 describe only HTTP callbacks and posting to a channel platform API with no mention of any model or AI component, so this requirement does not bear on this spoofed-callback threat.

req-AI-002 concerns validation of model output published externally. thr-001 describes callbacks being transformed into order-status messages by a conventional service (Channel Poster) and sent over HTTPS, with no model-generated output involved, so the requirement is not engaged by this threat.

req-AI-003 applies when customer content is sent to an external model provider. The evidence for Order Notifier (evd-001–evd-003) describes a payment provider callback and posting to a channel platform API, not to any model provider, so it does not bear on thr-001.

req-AI-004 concerns encoding of model output rendered into a UI or markup. thr-001 involves order-status callbacks being posted as messages to an operations channel via an HTTPS API (evd-003), with no model output in scope, so the requirement is not engaged.

req-AUTH-001 applies where user authentication is delegated to an external identity provider. thr-001 describes only machine-to-machine interaction between a payment provider, the Callback Receiver, and the Channel Poster (evd-001–evd-003), with no user authentication surface involved in the spoofed-callback path, so delegation of user authentication does not affect this threat.

req-AUTH-002 concerns multi-factor authentication for administrative or privileged access. The thr-001 attack path involves only an unauthenticated webhook endpoint and an internal posting service; no administrative or operator login is part of this scenario, so the requirement does not bear on this threat.

req-AUTHZ-001 addresses tenant-aware authorization in multi-tenant systems. thr-001 focuses on forged callbacks changing order status and channel messages (evd-001–evd-003) and does not describe any tenant boundary or cross-tenant data access; the core issue is lack of authenticity on the inbound webhook, so tenant separation is not engaged by this threat.

req-AUTHZ-002 concerns limiting delegated access to external platforms. While the Channel Poster calls a channel platform HTTPS API (evd-003), thr-001’s impact arises from the system using its ordinary ability to post messages when fed forged callbacks, not from over-broad or mis-scoped delegated privileges, so this requirement does not bear on the described spoofing threat.

req-CICD-001 covers how the deployment pipeline authenticates and manages third-party build components. thr-001 is a runtime spoofing attack against the Callback Receiver webhook endpoint and subsequent posting to a channel API (evd-002–evd-003); it does not involve the build or deployment path, so this requirement is not engaged.

req-DATA-001 addresses encryption of sensitive data in transit and at rest. thr-001 concerns integrity of order status callbacks and operations-channel messages being forged (evd-001–evd-003, evd-005); whether those flows are encrypted does not mitigate the ability to send unsigned but well-formed callbacks, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.

req-DATA-002 is about defining and enforcing retention for working copies of customer data. thr-001 describes immediate processing of callbacks into channel messages and does not involve retention of intermediate artifacts as the cause of the spoofing risk, so the requirement is not engaged by this threat.

req-DATA-003 concerns separation of stored artifacts by tenant in shared storage systems. thr-001 involves transient processing of payment provider callbacks into channel messages (evd-001–evd-003) and does not describe shared artifact storage or cross-tenant access; the problem is accepting unauthenticated callbacks, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.

req-DATA-004 addresses the ability to delete stored customer data across primary and derived stores. thr-001’s impact is that forged callbacks cause incorrect order statuses to be propagated into an operations channel (evd-001, evd-003, evd-005), not that data cannot be deleted on request, so the requirement is not engaged here.

req-LOG-001 covers exclusion of restricted data from logs and documentation of log destinations. thr-001 focuses on integrity of order status data and operations-channel messages resulting from forged callbacks (evd-001–evd-003, evd-005); the risk is not that sensitive data is logged or forwarded to a log platform, so this requirement does not bear on this threat.

req-LOG-002 applies where a system exposes an administrative or operator interface whose privileged actions must be audited. In thr-001, the only entry point is an automated payment provider callback endpoint (cmp-001) feeding an internal service (cmp-002) and then a channel API (cmp-004) (evd-001–evd-003, evd-005); no operator-driven administrative interface is involved, so this requirement is not engaged by the threat.

req-NET-001 concerns keeping internal data stores, queues, caches, or internal services off untrusted networks. The vulnerable component in thr-001 is the Callback Receiver webhook endpoint (cmp-001), which is explicitly an internet-exposed endpoint registered with the payment provider and accepting requests from anywhere (evd-002, evd-005); it is a public interface by design rather than an internal component, so this requirement does not bear on this threat.

req-SECRET-001 applies where the system holds long-lived signing keys or provider credentials and describes how they are stored. thr-001’s spoofing path uses the system’s ordinary ability to post to the channel platform once a callback is accepted (evd-003, evd-005); it does not involve compromise, misuse, or storage of outbound credentials, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.

req-SECRET-002 addresses whether credentials used to access customer resources on external platforms are short-lived. In thr-001, the attacker abuses an unauthenticated inbound callback endpoint to cause the system to perform normal posting work; the attack does not depend on credential lifetime or revocation, so this requirement is not engaged by the described spoofing threat.

req-TPI-001 concerns documentation of how external processors retain and use customer data. Although the Channel Poster sends order-status updates to a channel platform API (evd-003), thr-001’s impact is that those messages may contain forged statuses due to unauthenticated callbacks; it does not turn on the channel provider’s retention or secondary use of the data, so this requirement does not bear on this threat.

req-TPI-002 applies where externally triggered work that consumes metered resources must be bounded. thr-001 describes forged callbacks causing incorrect but ordinary-cost order-status postings to the operations channel (evd-001–evd-003, evd-006), with the concern being integrity of updates rather than unbounded consumption of a metered external service, so this requirement does not bear on the threat as stated.

req-WEBHOOK-001 applies where the system exposes an endpoint that accepts events from an external platform and performs privileged work based on them. In thr-001, the Callback Receiver (cmp-001) is an endpoint registered with the payment provider that processes any well-formed callback it receives (evd-002, evd-005) and drives order-status updates that are propagated to an operations channel (evd-001–evd-003), so inbound event authenticity is directly relevant to the threat.

req-WEBHOOK-002 concerns preventing or safely handling replay of previously valid inbound events once their authenticity has been verified. In thr-001, the documentation states that callbacks are not signed and the provider’s signing feature is not enabled (evd-002, evd-005), so there is no authenticity verification in place; the described impact arises from accepting entirely forged but well-formed callbacks rather than from replaying genuine ones, so replay-handling does not bear on this specific threat.
